record.title: China’s CAC proposes cooperation on intelligent-internet infrastructure and agent interoperability
record.summary: On 4 November 2026, China’s Cyberspace Administration published a cooperation initiative on intelligent internet development. Its eight proposals address network and compute infrastructure, agent interoperability standards and lifecycle trust, application ecosystems, cross-border data, safety, digital skills and multilateral governance dialogue. The text calls for open, non-discriminatory international standards for agent interoperability and a verifiable, traceable trust framework covering agent discovery, negotiation and execution. This is a nonbinding cooperation initiative: it does not establish adopted standards, binding duties, implementation or participating-body commitments. The official page was accessible through its indexed Chinese text, although direct page retrieval failed in this review.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: China’s Cyberspace Administration published an Intelligent Internet Innovation and Development Cooperation Initiative dated 4 November 2026 at 16:00 China Standard Time.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The initiative proposes cooperation across eight areas, including open and non-discriminatory international standards for agent interoperability and a verifiable, traceable trust framework covering agent discovery, negotiation and execution; it also addresses infrastructure connectivity, cross-border data flows, safety, digital skills and multilateral governance dialogue.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected initiative does not establish adopted standards, binding obligations, funded implementation, participating-body commitments or measured effects; its proposals are not evidence of operational agent interoperability or trust controls.

brief.title: China’s CAC proposes cooperation on intelligent-internet infrastructure and agent interoperability
brief.why_it_matters: The initiative places agent-to-agent interoperability, lifecycle trust and cross-border data flows within a broader infrastructure and governance proposal. If these proposals lead to formal standards work or coordinated implementation, they could shape how agent systems connect across platforms and jurisdictions. For now, the evidence establishes a published policy proposal, not adoption or practical effect.
